data.rule: Before starting the critic/rubber_duck gates, run `ddflow reviewers list` and confirm there is an ENABLED reviewer whose family differs from the author's. A reviewer with `gates = []` is disabled; roborev (or any same-family reviewer) does not satisfy the independence check even when it reviews the diff, and `ddflow complete` refuses on it with "--force overrides". If no different-family reviewer is enabled, ask the operator up front whether to enable one or to accept the coverage gap, rather than discovering it at completion time.
data.summary: Check `ddflow reviewers list` for an ENABLED, different-family reviewer before running critic/rubber_duck. A `gates = []` entry is disabled, and a same-family reviewer (or roborev) does not satisfy the independence check, so `complete` refuses and only `--force` gets past it. Ask the operator early.
data.title: Confirm an enabled different-family reviewer exists before the critic gates, not at completion
data.why: On B-dupes-sweep the only enabled reviewer (lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash) was the author's own family, and the alibaba Qwen was disabled by the operator's local config (gates = []). Three roborev rounds and a full suite were run before `complete` refused on independence, forcing a `--force` the operator had to authorize mid-task.

data.text: Housekeeping: research record Rbd13a36147 is a VOID placeholder created at the very start of this session by a malformed tool call (its only content is the question 'placeholder'); it should be ignored. The real research for this task is R-dupes-sweep (CONFIRMED). The log is append-only so it was not deleted.

data.summary: Implemented B-dupes-sweep: `ddflow dupes` (a pair sweep over the records already in the log, including removed items and forgotten memories, skipping pairs already linked/dismissed/superseded) and `ddflow link` (settle a pair; two lessons linked as duplicates merge via the existing --supersedes mechanism). Added MCP ddflow_dupes/ddflow_link, a dedupe_sweep workflow prompt, a bounded doctor note counting unsettled pairs, and README. Acceptance met: B203~B-semantic-recall found on the corpus snapshot (0.424), 72 of home-simulator's 86 LS-* lessons found at the show floor, and a --distinct pair never returns. Three roborev rounds (d5d98553/a68bee10/e288e225) found and I fixed: a link reason dropped by the fold projection, removed/forgotten pairs unsettleable, duplicated relation lists, an unbounded doctor sweep, a dismissal reason reaching no surface, and stale docs; the final head 1386b13b reviewed clean. Full suite 5848 passed on the final head; ci passed. Merged as 920e46ef. Cross-family critic/rubber_duck recorded UNAVAILABLE (the only other-family reviewer is disabled by the operator's local config; the operator chose to leave it and accept the gap), so complete was forced with the independence override recorded. Lesson L-check-cross-family-reviewer-before-gates captured.

data.claim: Nothing exists for included/remote config: no include, extends, preset, URL or org-policy mechanism (seams: tomlcfg.config_paths is the single ordered path list for foreign tables; Config.load hard-codes default->file->local->env; [prompts]/macro prompt_file/export template paths can already point outside the repo; lenient unknown keys exist for newer config). Provenance is the layer name only (no file, line or per-entry origin for gates/reviewers/companions/macros). Most config writes are NOT logged: knobs, gate defs, pipelines, rules (files only, no rule.* events), prompts, templates, macros, companions, hooks, adopt outputs; only flow choices, export selection, tool-written reviewers/approvals, cadence and knowledge records are evented. Parity gaps: workflow gate exposes a subset of GateDef and cannot target local; ddflow_export lacks local/lock/ack/eject; ddflow_prompts lacks force; companions_add lacks force; help pages cannot be ejected; prompts have no local layer; quota profiles have no CLI or MCP surface; reviewers add/presets/test are CLI-only; agents can loosen policy knobs over MCP (enforce.*, upgrade.skew, loops.*, gates.allow_skip_with_reason, lease.*) and uninstall hooks, guarded only by tool-description wording. Two bugs found and filed: the human-gate guard ignores promotion_pipeline (Be14f271da8); flow choose misreports in_effect under a local override (B025c8de942).
data.falsifier: A project inherits gates, rules, prompts and companions from a signed org bundle in a local bare repo; its own override wins for a default; an enforced floor refuses a lowering from CLI, MCP and a hand edit; an upstream change is detected, reviewed and applied only through the lock bump; replay shows which org revision governed each item.
data.mechanism: Prior art: Renovate presets (github>org/repo//path#tag, org config repo discovery, data-only, ignorePresets), pre-commit (repo+rev pinned, autoupdate --freeze to SHA), GitHub org .github defaults (whole-file override) and rulesets required workflows (enforced, evaluate mode), GitLab pipeline execution policies (separate policy project, isolated), Claude Code managed settings (managed > CLI > local > project > user; drop-in dir; server-managed polled hourly with cache, fail-open unless forceRemoteSettingsRefresh; lock keys strictest-wins; approval per hash for hooks), Codex managed_config.toml (defaults) vs requirements.toml (constraints), Gemini CLI system-defaults < user < project < system settings, Cursor team rules with enforce flag, OPA bundles (ETag polling, manifest revision/roots, signed per-file hashes, persist last good), Flux GitRepository (interval, ref, verify SSH/PGP, revision+digest, suspend), Kyverno enforce/audit, Terraform and Nix lock files. Design: [[org.source]] (project, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml, /etc/ddflow/org.toml) with git+https/git+ssh/https/file/gh: URIs, @ref and //profile; bundle mirrors .ddflow/ plus manifest.toml and policy.toml; committed .ddflow/org.lock (commit + canonical tree digest + signer); layers shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org enforced; policy kinds pin/floor/ceiling/require/allow with enforce|audit; per-key merge strategy; data vs executable tiers (executable needs per-hash approval); machine-level source allowlist; signatures required for enforced; update detection only, applied through a reviewed update task/PR; offline = locked cache, enforced fail-closed; per-value provenance and config.changed events for every surface.
data.probe: Code survey (config.py load/explain, tomlcfg, configwrite, workflow, reviewers, companions, prompts, export, flow, rules, macros, hooks, quota) + prior-art web survey.
data.probe_output: Confirmed by reading: configwrite in_pipeline omits promotion_pipeline; api/flow overridden omits local. No remote/include mechanism anywhere.
data.question: How can ddflow fetch configuration extensions (config, workflow, rules, skills, companions, prompts, templates, doc types, schedules, everything configurable) from git, HTTPS or another source, sync them periodically, use them as defaults unless the project overrides them (and enforce some as policy), and give every configurable thing parity across MCP, prompt, CLI and files with changes preserved?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-05 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): retrieve configuration extensions of config, workflow, rules, skills, companions -- everything configurable -- from git, remote HTTPS or another source, sync them periodically, so a company manages defaults, policies, rules, skills and workflows centrally and the project uses them unless the user overrides; and use the opportunity to ensure parity: everything configurable through MCP, prompt, CLI or config files, and preserved, behind a unified interface; check how similar software does it. Research R-org-config (CONFIRMED). TODAY: no include/extends/remote mechanism; provenance is a layer name; most config writes are not logged; parity gaps listed in R-org-config; agents can loosen policy knobs over MCP. DESIGN: sources [[org.source]] in the project, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml or /etc/ddflow/org.toml (git+https, git+ssh, https tarball, file, gh:owner/repo//profile@ref); a bundle mirrors .ddflow/ plus manifest.toml and policy.toml; committed .ddflow/org.lock (commit + canonical digest + signer); layers shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org ENFORCED (policy kinds pin/floor/ceiling/require/allow, mode enforce|audit -- after Codex requirements.toml, Claude managed settings, Kyverno); per-key merge strategy from knob metadata; data applied once verified, executable content (commands, hooks, MCP launch lines, command reviewers, skill scripts) only after a per-hash operator approval; sources must be on a machine-level allowlist and enforced content must be signed; sync DETECTS upstream changes and proposes a reviewed lock bump (task or PR), never silently applies (except signed enforced policy if the org opts in, recorded); offline runs from the locked cache, enforced policy fails closed; per-value provenance (layer, source, rev, file, line) and config.changed events for every write on every surface. Depends on P-unify (D-unify-first): knob metadata (B-uni-knobs), overlay loader (B-uni-overlay), def-records, record surface and command registry, approval, local worker and trigger engine. Order: decide -> {sources, bundle} -> lock -> trust -> layers -> policy -> {events, provenance} -> {sync, parity, agent-guard} -> kinds -> {authoring, surfaces} -> acceptance.
data.title: Central configuration: a company's defaults and policies (config, workflow, rules, skills, companions, prompts, templates, doc types, schedules) fetched from git or HTTPS, pinned, verified, synced and layered under the project's overrides -- and every configurable thing on every surface, recorded

data.body: Ask the operator and record D-org-config with the R-org-config recommendations as defaults: (1) [[org.source]] {name, uri, ref, profile, verify, refresh, required} in project config.toml, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml, /etc/ddflow/org.toml (and DDFLOW_ORG_CONFIG); (2) layers shipped < org defaults (declaration order) < project < local < env/CLI < org enforced; (3) enforced lives only in a bundle's policy.toml: pin, floor, ceiling, require, allow; mode enforce|audit per item; the shipped kernel rules expressed the same way; (4) .ddflow/org.lock committed; pins move only via `ddflow org update`, which files an update task (or PR when [flow].integration=pr); signed enforced policy may auto-apply if the source sets auto_apply=enforced, recorded as an event; (5) a source must be allowlisted at machine/system level before a project can use it; enforced content must verify (SSH allowed_signers for git tags/commits first, minisign for tarballs, sigstore optional); TOFU only interactively with the fingerprint shown; (6) executable content needs a per-hash operator approval, re-asked on change; D-reviewer-trust unchanged; (7) offline: run from the locked cache; locked digest missing: defaults fall back to shipped with a loud warning, enforced fails closed for claim/merge/complete (on_unavailable=open opt-out); (8) syncable kinds: knobs, gates, pipelines, reviewers (non-command), companions catalog and allow list, rules, prompts and commands, help, macros, export templates and selection, doc types, schedules, triggers, subagent roles, skills, harness descriptors, id schemes; (9) auto-discovery of <org>/ddflow-config only proposes, never adds.
data.title: Operator decisions for central configuration: source syntax and locations, layer order, enforced policy kinds and audit mode, lock and update flow (task/PR vs auto-apply), trust (allowlist, signatures, TOFU), executable-content approval, offline behaviour, which kinds are syncable

data.body: Parse and validate sources (refuse unknown schemes, credentials in URLs, path escapes); git via infra/git (B-uni-proc): `git ls-remote` to resolve ref, shallow + sparse fetch of the profile path into a temp dir, then move into ~/.cache/ddflow/org/<sha256>/ (atomic, B-uni-fsio); HTTPS via urllib with If-None-Match/ETag, size cap, tar/zip extraction refusing symlinks, absolute paths and '..'; file:// for monorepos and tests. Canonical digest = sha256 over sorted (path, mode, sha256(content)) so it is stable across git versions and archive formats. Credentials come from git's own helpers / netrc, never from ddflow config. Tests with a local bare repo, an HTTP test server, malicious archives.
data.title: Source spec and fetchers: [[org.source]] in project, user and system files; URIs git+https, git+ssh, https tarball/zip, file://, gh:owner/repo; @ref (tag, semver range, sha) and //profile subpaths; shallow sparse git fetch and HTTP with ETag; content-addressed cache shared across projects; canonical tree digest

data.body: One loader per kind already exists or is planned on the overlay loader (B-uni-overlay); the bundle reader hands each subtree to that kind's loader as one more layer, so a bundle can carry anything a project can. manifest.roots declares which kinds/namespaces the bundle owns, so two bundles cannot both define the same enforced item (OPA roots); min_ddflow_version refuses a too-old ddflow with the upgrade remedy. Unknown keys in a bundle newer than the code follow the lenient rule (warn, skip) for defaults and fail-closed for policy.
data.title: Bundle format: a directory mirroring .ddflow/ (config.toml, gates.toml, reviewers.toml, companions.toml, macros.toml, rules/, prompts/, help/, templates/export/, doctypes/, schedules/, triggers/, agents/, skills/, harnesses/, ids.toml) plus manifest.toml (name, revision, roots, min_ddflow_version, schema_version) and policy.toml; per-kind validation with file:line

data.body: Terraform/Nix model: a moving ref never changes behaviour by itself. A missing cache entry re-fetches exactly the locked commit and verifies the digest; a mismatch is refused (exit 3) and reported, never used. merge=union is wrong for a lock; a merge conflict in org.lock is resolved by `ddflow org update` (documented, and doctor detects conflict markers).
data.title: Lock file .ddflow/org.lock (committed): per source the requested ref, resolved commit, canonical digest, signer, fetched_at and kinds; resolution always from the lock; digest verified on every load; ddflow org add/remove/update are the only ways a pin moves

data.body: A project cannot introduce a source the machine does not allow (otherwise a cloned repo could name an attacker's 'org'): the allowlist lives in ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml or /etc/ddflow/org.toml, never in the project. Verification uses git's own `verify-tag`/`verify-commit` with gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile from the source's verify block. Executable content -- gate commands, companion install commands, hooks, MCP server launch lines, command reviewers, macros with commands, doc-type cmd: sources, skills with scripts, schedule job commands -- is inert until `ddflow org approve` (person only; B-uni-approval) records approval of its digest; a changed digest asks again. Instruction text (rules, prompts, help) is data. Each refusal names the item, source and digest.
data.title: Trust and verification: a machine/system allowlist of source URIs, signature verification (SSH allowed_signers for git tags or commits, minisign for archives, sigstore optional; external binary missing = unavailable), TOFU only interactively, and data vs executable tiers with per-hash operator approval for executable content

data.body: Today Config.load hard-codes default -> file -> local -> env and tomlcfg.config_paths separately orders foreign tables; recorded flow choices are a third mechanism. Replace with one LayerStack whose entries carry (layer, source, rev, path) so provenance falls out. Lists: append + dedupe by default; a project writes `extend-<key>` to add or `<key>.replace = true` to replace (Ruff model); pipelines and fallback chains are ordered and replaced whole; named assets (rules/<id>, prompts/<name>) replace whole by id. Behaviour without any org source is byte-identical to today (golden of `ddflow config --explain`).
data.title: Layered resolution for everything: one ordered layer stack (shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org enforced) used by Config.load, the foreign tables (gates, reviewers, companions, macros) and every overlay asset; merge strategy per key declared in knob metadata (replace, deep-merge, append-dedupe with extend-/replace operators, ordered-chain replace, named-asset replace by id)

data.body: Examples: floor review.min_other_family_reviewers=1; require gates.task_pipeline contains [critic, unit_tests]; pin enforce.commit_without_lease=block; allow companions=[roborev, codeguide-mcp]; allow reviewer models; require rules/security-baseline. A violating write from CLI, MCP, prompt or configure is refused (exit 3) naming the policy item, source and rev; a hand-edited file that violates is reported by doctor and, in enforce mode, claim/merge/complete refuse until fixed; audit mode only reports (brief + doctor). The four enforced kernel rules, human gates and D-reviewer-trust are re-expressed as shipped policy so the org layer extends one mechanism. A project-level policy file lets the operator lock a key locally the same way (generalising export disable --lock).
data.title: Enforced policy: policy.toml items (pin, floor, ceiling, require, allow) with enforce|audit, applied last; violations refused at write time on every surface and at load for hand edits; required assets cannot be shadowed; invalid enforced values fail closed; ddflow's own kernel rules shipped as the same policy

data.body: Today only flow choices, export selection, tool-written reviewers and approvals are evented; knob writes, gate defs, pipelines, rules (files only), prompts, templates, macros, companions, hooks and adopt outputs are not. Add one event family (on the def-records envelope, B-uni-def-records) written by the single config writer so every surface records it identically; values redacted and large text stored as digest + committed file path; the git-ignored local layer recorded as digest only. org.source.added/removed/updated/fetched/verified/failed and org.policy.applied for the org lifecycle. `ddflow replay` and `ddflow history config <key>` show who changed what, when, through which surface and why.
data.title: Every configuration change preserved: config.changed events (key or asset, layer, old/new digest, by, surface cli|mcp|prompt|file-edit, reason) for knobs, gates, pipelines, reviewers, rules, prompts, templates, macros, companions, hooks and org sources; hand edits detected by digest at load and recorded; replay rebuilds the configuration history

data.body: Like git config --show-origin but per key with revision: `gates.task_pipeline: acme@3f2a1c policy.toml:12 (enforced) <- project config.toml:40 (ignored: locked)`. Doctor: lock status, last fetch outcome, pending upstream update, audit violations, executable content awaiting approval, cache missing. claim/complete/gate events record org revisions so replay knows which policy governed each item.
data.title: Explain any value: per-value provenance (layer, source, rev, file, line) for knobs, table entries (gates, reviewers, companions, macros) and assets; ddflow config explain <key|asset> prints the override chain; config show --resolved --json; doctor 'Org sources' section; item and gate events carry the policy revision in force

data.body: Detection runs in the background worker's budget (B-uni-local-worker) and the schedule/trigger engine (B-uni-triggers) -- no private timer. `org diff` resolves the config with the candidate revision in a temp layer stack and prints changed knobs, added/removed/changed assets, new executable content needing approval and new policy violations the project would hit. `org update` creates a task whose deliverable is the org.lock bump plus any project fixes, gated like any change; with integration=pr it opens a PR. Signed enforced policy with auto_apply=enforced applies immediately and records org.policy.applied. Offline or fetch failure: keep last known good, note it, never treat 'could not fetch' as 'no policy'.
data.title: Periodic sync that proposes, never surprises: check each source on its refresh interval (jittered) and at brief through the tick/trigger engine; git ls-remote / HTTP ETag; a newer revision appears in the brief with a diff summary; ddflow org diff shows the effective change per key and asset; ddflow org update files a reviewed update task or PR bumping org.lock

data.body: Built on the command registry and record surface (B-uni-cmd-core, B-uni-record-surface). Every row of the R-org-config inventory becomes a target; a target an agent may not change (human gates, command reviewers, approvals, export lock/ack, policy) is exposed on MCP as an explained refusal (exit 3, 'operator only: run ... yourself') rather than missing, and listed as data (operator_only=True) instead of parity-test exemption tables. Every write goes through the one writer (B-org-events) so it is validated against policy and recorded. A /configure prompt walks the operator through any target in plain words. Each target can be authored for project, local or an org bundle (`--layer org --bundle <dir>`).
data.title: One configuration interface on every surface: a registry of configurable targets (kind, layer, schema, writer, operator_only) generates CLI, MCP, the /configure prompt and file docs from one declaration, with a generated parity test; close the gaps found: full gate definitions and local layer in workflow_*, export local/lock/ack/eject, prompts force and local layer, help eject, companions_add force, reviewers add/presets/test over MCP, quota profiles surface, rules as recorded events

data.body: Today only tool-description wording stops an agent from setting enforce.commit_without_lease=off or uninstalling hooks over MCP; the review-budget case writes a session note. Mark knobs with tier=policy in their metadata; an agent write becomes a pending config proposal (event) shown in brief and doctor until a person approves (B-uni-approval) or rejects; refuse mode refuses outright; allow keeps today's behaviour. Org policy can pin the mode.
data.title: Agents cannot quietly loosen policy: knobs marked policy (enforce.*, upgrade.skew, loops.*, gates.allow_skip_with_reason, lease.*, hook uninstall, review budgets) are proposed, not applied, when an agent changes them; the operator confirms; [policy].agent_changes = propose|refuse|allow

data.body: Each kind registers with the overlay loader once (B-uni-overlay); this task proves each one resolves from an org bundle, is overridable by the project unless required by policy, reports provenance, and that executable parts stay inert until approved. Skills from an org bundle reuse the skills install/lock path (B-skills-install) rather than a second installer. Org-required companions appear in the brief's companion line with the source named.
data.title: Every syncable kind wired to the layer stack: rules, prompts and commands, help, macros, export templates and selection, doc types, schedules and triggers, subagent roles, skills (with the skills lock), companions catalog and allow list, harness descriptors, id schemes, reviewers (non-command)

data.body: The guide covers hosting as a git repository (tags, signed with SSH keys), as static HTTPS archives with minisign, internal mirrors, profiles per project type (//python, //service), staged rollout with audit mode, and rotating signing keys.
data.title: Tooling for the people who run the central configuration: ddflow org init (scaffold a policy repo), org lint (validate a bundle), org test <project> (resolve against a project: what changes, what would be violated), org export (lift a project's configuration into a bundle), and a hosting and signing guide

data.body: Generated from the command registry; CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test); exit codes 0/1/2/3 as everywhere.
data.title: ddflow org on every surface: sources list/add/remove, status, diff, update, approve (person only), explain, lint, init, test, export; MCP ddflow_org (read, diff, propose; changes that need a person are explained refusals); /org prompt; help topic; README section and knob counts

data.body: Also: without any org source, ddflow's behaviour and `config --explain` output are byte-identical to before (golden). No repository-specific names (test_repo_is_generic).
data.title: Acceptance: a signed org bundle in a local bare repo configures a throwaway project end to end -- defaults inherited and overridden, an enforced floor refusing a lowering from CLI, MCP and a hand edit, executable content inert until approved, an upstream change detected and applied only through the reviewed lock bump, offline from cache, fail-closed without it, replay naming the revision
